annotation_policy: There are 44 original annotation rows for 44 distinct source verses, without duplicate selection. All44 original rectangles were inspected and retained. Neighbouring text can fall inside a rectangle, while marginal additions may lie outside. sourceWitness=LL and panelId are annotation provenance only; no LL text was consulted.

notes.evidence: A large ornamental Q opens the poem. The first two verses remain source lines, not a prose heading.

The n of Omina is darker. A dark horizontal stroke lies between concinuistis and aues, with a crossing upright near the next word. These do not establish an erased recoverable word. A question-like sign closes the verse.
The ending ere of occurrere is darker. Source occurrence and spelling are retained without reconstructing an earlier state.
The b of bella is dark; the current word is readable.
A long rising stroke after mihi extends into the right margin. It is retained schematically with unspecified function.
The a of erat is dark. The source verb prostitit is retained without normalization.
The compact dark group after quid appears enim, though overlapping strokes make its exact division uncertain. It remains unclear. A small right-margin cross has unspecified function.
A slender vertical mark crosses Me. It is recorded without cancelling the letters. The et ending of placet is a ligature.

Slender vertical strokes follow thebe, the et ligature of foret, and acta, with another near the cum/thebe interval. The principal boundary marks are recorded schematically; the text remains uncancelled.
Final it of mouit is darker. A small terminal vertical mark is recorded with unspecified function.
The source reads Auersis. Its ordinary letter forms are represented with standard characters, not normalized to a different opening.
The ending of destituisse is followed by a short dark stroke and a wide space before opus. The readable word is retained without reconstructing an erased ending.

An i is written above the a-region of main-line Malueram; the baseline remains visible and no complete cancellation is asserted. Debuerat is written in the left margin, preceded by small marks of uncertain function. A vertical stroke crosses uerbis.
The n of nos is dark. Scilla is preserved with its source spelling.
A slender stroke crosses the premit/rapidos boundary. It does not securely cancel either word.
The source reads Victor abantia desultat. A short horizontal mark follows abantia and a vertical stroke crosses desultat; no normalized replacement is supplied.
The source name appears tityon. A slender terminal stroke has unspecified function.
The source writes uipero without a separate e after r. That r is darker. The spelling is retained.

The verse opens the new page with Fecimus. Paired oblique left-margin strokes also recur beside verses29,31,32,36 and37; they are documented as marginal marks without assigning them a textual function.
The opening group appears Adiol and remains unclear; the following it of ithacis is dark. No familiar name is substituted for the visible source sequence.
The initial source word is Proditor, retained without normalization.
The final m of niobem is crossed horizontally and retained as del. A single f followed by a point stands after silicem; fecimus is an explicitly tentative expansion. The later fecimus is written out.

Concit has a bar and dark t, explicitly expanded Concinit. The following dark ot begins otrisium. After cecropi there is a horizontal stroke and then salesitum, with a crossing stroke and dark i-region. This unusual source sequence is retained without restoring an expected name or word.
The au of aues is dark. Source aues is retained; no former letters are supplied.
A vertical stroke follows referam. The final dentes has dark overlapping letters, so its current reading remains qualified without supplying an earlier word.
Final i of Qui, uom of uomerent, e of ore and initial b of bobes are darker. Bobes is retained without normalizing its consonant.
The source reads Flere genus electra tuas aurora sorores. Ga is added above the ending area of aurora. The baseline is retained without claiming cancellation or silently creating a normalized name.
The initial word is Quaeq followed by a point, with no distinct terminal que sign. It is retained without inventing an expansion mark.

Final s of mensis is dark and followed by horizontal marks over a pale space. The visible current word and marks are retained without asserting erasure or reconstructing missing letters. The source writes furalibus.
Fac followed by a short stroke is written above iucunda. It is encoded as an unexpanded abbreviation; its intended full word and relationship to the baseline adjective are not assumed.
The source reads Obligat historica nec sua uerba fide. Its word order is retained.
A point follows Faemina. The et ending of nocet is a ligature; a colon-like sign and terminal stroke separate the next poem, whose initial C begins below.
